newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain savings banks bid for 19.4 pct of Ebro - press.
newsitem.headline: Spain savings banks bid for 19.4 pct of Ebro - press.

text.p: Savings banks in Spain's Castille-Leon region are to present an offer to buy 19.4 percent of sugar firm Ebro Agricolas from the Kuwait Investment Office (KIO) for a total 20.0 billion pesetas, local press reports said on Friday.

The regional economy department was reported to be backing the offer by savings banks Caja Espana, Caja de Ahorros de Avila, Caja Burgos, Caja de Ahorros del Circulo Catolico and Caja Segovia, having negotiated it with them.
The offer would value Ebro at a price of 3,000 pesetas per share, the report said.
No-one at the regional government or the savings banks was immediately available to comment.

The reports said the savings banks would buy 19.4 percent from KIO which currently owns 39 percent. This would add to stakes already held by Caja de Salamanca y Soria and by Caja Espana, for a total 24.5 percent savings' bank stake, keeping the firm in Spanish hands.
Apart from its Ebro stake, KIO also owns 21 percent of sugar firm Azucarera with which Ebro started talks on a merger last year.
France's Saint Louis Generale Sucriere, which holds stakes in both Azucarera and Ebro, has expressed interest in controlling the new Spanish sugar group.
The savings banks' agreement may be announced in August, the reports said.
